steps.instruction: Add a new variant `{ kind: "clear" }` to the Command union. It has no other fields. Leave everything else unchanged.
steps.interfaceChange: export type Command = { kind: "add"; title: string; due?: string; } | { kind: "complete"; id: number; } | { kind: "list"; } | { kind: "clear"; };

steps.instruction: Add a 'clear' command that removes completed todos. The Todo type has no `completed` field; a todo counts as completed when its `done` field is true. (1) Export a pure function `clear(todos: Todo[]): Todo[]`. It returns a new array with only the todos where done !== true, keeps their original order, and does not mutate the input array or its items. (2) The types unit is adding a new Command variant `{ kind: "clear" }` in this same round. parseArgs must return `{ kind: "clear" }` when the command word is "clear", reading argv the same way it already reads the other command words. (3) For `{ kind: "clear" }`, run(path, cmd) loads todos from path, applies clear, saves the result back to path, and returns a short message saying how many were removed, e.g. `Cleared 2 completed todos`. Add unit tests for these in commands.test.ts.
steps.interfaceChange: export declare function clear(todos: Todo[]): Todo[];

input.reason: The Todo type has no 'completed' field, so I'm reading "completed" as `done === true`, which is what the existing complete command sets. That means adding a clear variant to Command in types, plus a clear function in commands and handling for it in parseArgs and run.
